Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
The -s ending on a verb marks singular in the present tense, which is the opposite of the noun, where -s marks plural: the driver drives, the drivers drive.
Read it aloud, then record yourself: the main stress falls on the content word, not on the hedge.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Subject-Predicate Agreement.

Find the head noun, then make the verb agree with it. Intervening phrases starting with of, with, together with, as well as and including never change the number: the list of candidates was, not were.

the list of + plural noun — singular verb: the list of candidates was published
a number of + plural noun — plural verb: a number of complaints have been resolved
the number of + plural noun — singular verb: the number of complaints has fallen
neither X nor Y — verb agrees with Y: neither the manager nor the drivers were informed
each of / one of — singular verb: each of the proposals needs a budget
collective noun — singular body, plural members: the committee has decided / the team are arguing
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'The number of applications ___ risen.'
2. Complete: 'Neither the chair nor the members ___ replied.'
3. Which sentence is correct?
options: The team is arguing among themselves.
The team are arguing among themselves.
Both are defensible in British English.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

The number of complaints — has fallen sharply. (The head is number, singular.)
A number of complaints — have been resolved. (Here a number of means several.)
The team — are arguing among themselves. (British English allows a plural verb for a group in dispute.)
What do you observe?

The verb agrees with the head of the subject, whatever sits between the two. Prepositional phrases, relative clauses and lists are noise. Collective nouns take a singular verb when they act as one body and a plural verb when the members act separately.
1. Which word decides the verb in 'the list of candidates'?
2. Is 'a number of complaints have' correct?
options: Yes: a number of means several.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can keep subjects and verbs in agreement.

Success criteria:
- I can find the head of a long subject.
- I can keep the verb singular after each of and the number of.
- I can choose singular or plural after a collective noun on purpose.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ The list of candidates were published (verb agrees with candidates) → ✅ The list of candidates was published
❌ Each of the proposals need a budget (plural verb after each) → ✅ Each of the proposals needs a budget
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

was submitted late.
is still under review.
supports that conclusion.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where relative clauses: review and deepening carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
